q.t: How many faces does a cube have?
q.e: Top, bottom, front, back, left and right — like the six faces of a dice.

q.t: How many edges does a cube have?
q.e: 4 around the top, 4 around the bottom and 4 upright ones joining them.

q.t: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have?
q.e: 4 corners on the top face and 4 on the bottom face.

q.t: A brick has the shape of a:
q.e: It has 6 rectangular faces with length, breadth and height all different.

q.t: How many vertices does a cone have?
q.e: Only the pointed tip (the apex). The circular edge has no corners.

q.t: How many curved surfaces does a cylinder have?
q.e: One curved surface wrapped around, plus two flat circular ends.

q.t: How many edges does a sphere have?
q.e: A sphere is one smooth curved surface — no flat faces, so nothing meets to form an edge.

q.t: How many faces does a triangular pyramid (tetrahedron) have?
q.e: A triangular base plus three triangular side faces.

q.t: A dice has the shape of a:
q.e: All six faces are equal squares.

q.t: How many faces does a square pyramid have?
q.e: One square base and four triangular faces meeting at the top.

q.t: Euler’s formula for any polyhedron is:
q.e: Check with a cube: 6 faces + 8 vertices − 12 edges = 2. It works for every solid with flat faces.

q.t: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
q.e: 2 triangular ends and 3 rectangular sides.

q.t: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
q.e: 3 on each triangular end (6) plus 3 joining the ends.

q.t: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
q.e: 3 corners on each of the two triangular ends.

q.t: How many edges does a square pyramid have?
q.e: 4 around the square base and 4 slanting up to the top.

q.t: The net of a cube is made of how many squares?
q.e: A net is the solid unfolded flat, so it needs one square for each of the 6 faces.

q.t: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
q.e: The two circular ends.

q.t: A cuboid has how many pairs of identical opposite faces?
q.e: Top–bottom, front–back and left–right.

q.t: How many edges does a tetrahedron have?
q.e: 3 around the base and 3 rising to the top. Check Euler: 4 + 4 − 6 = 2 ✓.

q.t: How many surfaces (flat and curved together) does a cone have?
q.e: One flat circular base and one curved surface.

q.t: A polyhedron has 7 faces and 10 vertices. How many edges does it have?
q.e: Euler: F + V − E = 2, so E = 7 + 10 − 2 = 15. (It is a pentagonal prism.)

q.t: A polyhedron has 8 faces and 12 edges. How many vertices does it have?
q.e: V = 2 + E − F = 2 + 12 − 8 = 6. (An octahedron.)

q.t: On a dice, opposite faces add up to 7. Which number is opposite 3?
How many faces does a pentagonal prism have?
q.e: 2 pentagonal ends plus 5 rectangular sides.

q.t: How many vertices does a hexagonal pyramid have?
q.e: 6 corners on the hexagonal base plus the apex.

q.t: A cylinder is cut by a plane parallel to its base. The cross-section is a:
q.e: Every slice parallel to the base is a copy of the circular base.

q.t: A cylinder standing upright is cut straight down through its centre. The cross-section is a:
q.e: The cut has the two straight sides of the cylinder as its height and the diameter as its width.

q.t: Looking straight down on a cone standing on its base, the top view is a:
q.e: From above you see the outline of the circular base (with the tip as a point at the centre).

q.t: A lamp shines on a ball. The shadow of the ball on a wall straight behind it is a:
q.e: A shadow is flat (2-D). A sphere has a circular outline from every direction.

q.t: How many edges does a pentagonal pyramid have?
q.e: 5 around the base and 5 slanting up to the apex.

q.t: Can a polyhedron have 10 faces, 20 edges and 15 vertices?
o: No, because F + V − E = 5, not 2
q.e: Every polyhedron must satisfy Euler’s formula: 10 + 15 − 20 = 5 ≠ 2.

q.t: A prism has 10 faces. How many edges does it have?
q.e: Two of the faces are the ends, so the base has 8 sides (octagon). A prism has 3 edges for every side of the base: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24.

q.t: A pyramid has 12 edges. How many faces does it have?
q.e: A pyramid has 2 edges for each side of its base, so the base has 6 sides. Faces = 6 triangles + 1 base = 7.

q.t: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube is painted on the outside and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 painted faces?
q.e: Those are the middle cubes of each edge (corners have 3, face-centres have 1). A cube has 12 edges with one such cube each.

q.t: A 3 × 3 × 3 cube is painted on the outside and cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have NO paint at all?
q.e: Only the cube hidden at the very centre. Check: 8 corners + 12 edge cubes + 6 face-centres + 1 = 27.

q.t: A solid has 6 vertices and 9 edges. What is it?
q.e: Faces = 2 + E − V = 2 + 9 − 6 = 5. A triangular prism has 5 faces, 6 vertices and 9 edges.

q.t: What is the total number of dots on all six faces of a dice?
q.e: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21. (Three opposite pairs that each add to 7.)

q.t: A cone is cut straight down through its tip and the centre of its base. The cross-section is a:
q.e: The cut shows the two slanting sides meeting at the tip, with the diameter of the base as the third side.

q.t: How many edges meet at each vertex of a cube?
q.e: One along the length, one along the breadth and one along the height.

q.t: What is the smallest number of faces a polyhedron can have?
q.e: You need at least 3 faces meeting at a point and one more to close the solid — the tetrahedron.
